content.thinking:
I'm going through each claim now. The root cause claim, that the payment provider began returning an error code to card lookups, checks out against the logs. The payment provider client then turned each of those responses into an exception, which is why the account page request failed instead of rendering. The plain-language version of the cause holds up as well.

I'm checking the remaining claims against the record. The "still at risk" point is hedged and holds, since the service wasn't back to normal by the time the incident was stopped. The symptom and the account page errors starting at onset are supported, and the failed requests look like failed card lookups. I'm also confirming that the earlier errors came before onset and that the next minute shows account pages rendering normally.

I'm checking the remaining contributing factors against the record: the nobody-paged point and the alert timing both line up, and since none of the claims call for a judgment beyond what the record shows, everything here stands as supported.

supported.quote: The third-party payment provider io-pay began returning {Gbf7d.1} to io-shop's card lookups for shoppers.
io-shop's payment provider client (payment_provider.py) raised each of those responses as PaymentProviderFailed, and the account page request failed with it instead of rendering.

The outside company that handles the shop's payments began refusing the shop's requests to look up shoppers' saved cards, and each time that happened the shop's account page failed along with the lookup.
Account pages could keep failing for as long as io-pay keeps refusing card lookups, and any later io-pay outage could fail them the same way.
rows: The service was not back to normal by 2026-11-12T17:24:21Z

supported.quote: Account page requests errored from the onset onward.

The failed account page requests were failed card lookups. io-shop's payment provider client raised PaymentProviderFailed when its call for a shopper's card failed, and the page request failed with it.
The card lookups failed because io-pay, the third-party payment provider that IO Payments Ltd runs, began returning {Gbf7d.1} for them at the onset.
The record does not show why io-pay failed.
Shoppers closing the connection (ClientDisconnected). Those errors came before the onset, and the next minute's log line shows account pages rendering normally.
No fallback was seen for when io-pay's card lookup fails. The account page request failed outright rather than rendering without the card details.
Account pages could still have rendered for shoppers while io-pay returned errors, with only the card details missing, so the outage would have been contained.
The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one

supported.quote: A person would have learned of the outage when the alert fired and could have asked IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay sooner, which would have shortened the incident.
